paragraphs: The CLK 200 has been part of the CLK range since 1997, spanning two generations under one badge. Early cars (C208, 1997 to 2003) use the M111 — a 1.8- to 2.3-litre 4-cylinder petrol engine shared across a wide range of Mercedes models of that era. From 2002, the C209-generation CLK 200 switched to the M271, a newer 4-cylinder petrol unit with its own documented wear pattern. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear patterns differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting. The CLK 200 is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CLK 200 on the road.

A 1.8-litre 4-cylinder petrol engine fitted to the CLK 200 from 2002 to 2009. Known for timing chain stretch and balance shaft issues — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, timing gears and gaskets as standard on every M271 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the CLK 200 spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M111 part will work on an M271 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic CLK quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
